content.title: Definition of PINCH
content.text: transitive verb 1 a : to squeeze between the finger and thumb or between the jaws of an instrument b : to prune the tip of (a plant or shoot) usually to induce branching c : to squeeze or compress painfully d : to cause physical or mental pain to e(1) : to cause to appear thin, haggard, or shrunken (2) : to cause to shrivel or wither 2 a : to subject to strict economy or want : straiten b : to restrain or limit narrowly : constrict 4 : to sail too close to the wind 2 b : as much as may be taken between the finger and thumb 3 : a marked thinning of a vein or bed Synonyms of pinch Choose the Right Synonym for pinch an important juncture in our country's history exigency stresses the pressure of restrictions or urgency of demands created by a special situation. emergency applies to a sudden unforeseen situation requiring prompt action to avoid disaster. the presence of mind needed to deal with emergencies contingency implies an emergency or exigency that is regarded as possible but uncertain of occurrence. pinch implies urgency or pressure for action to a less intense degree than exigency or emergency. strait, now commonly straits, applies to a troublesome situation from which escape is extremely difficult. crisis applies to a juncture whose outcome will make a decisive difference. Examples of pinch in a Sentence Verb My little brother is always trying to pinch me. He pinched her cheeks and told her how cute she was. Pinch together the edges of the dough.
